heading: The deferred storage and samples-plane capabilities
text:
### The deferred storage and samples-plane capabilities [LCAP.2.10]

Four construct capabilities gate constructs of the storage layer, which is
not part of this edition ([LSTO.2], [LSTO.3], [LHYD.1]):

| Capability | Would permit |
|---|---|
| `sampled_slots` | the `sampled` marker on a schema slot, routing its values to the samples plane |
| `persist_on_series` | `persist <dur>` on a series declaration, writing through to the samples plane |
| `storage_hydrate_facts` | bringing stored facts back as facts |
| `storage_hydrate_samples` | bringing sample history back as facts |

They stay in the registry ([LCAP.1]), so their names and numbers keep their
meaning for the edition that adds the storage layer. In this edition every
program and every dialect sets each of them `false`. The compiler **must**
refuse, with `DS_VALIDATE_CAPABILITY_DEFERRED`, a `use` block line setting
one `true` ([LDIA.3.3.7]) and a dialect definition whose `settings` set one
`true` ([NDLC.6.1]). A line or a setting naming one `false` is accepted.

No artefact the compiler accepts therefore enables or requires any of them,
and a runtime need contain no code for them.

alloy.name: lcap_2_10__deferred
alloy.note: The four capabilities of the clause's table, transcribed. The refusal of a use line or dialect setting one true (DS_VALIDATE_CAPABILITY_DEFERRED) is not modelled, as LCAP.2.1.5's is not: the model states the algebra of the settings.

alloy.name: lcap_2_10__written_dialects_set_the_deferred_false
alloy.note: Every dialect the corpus writes out (base, default, realtime, frame) sets each of the four false: the transcriptions of LDIA.9 and NDLC.2.1 against the clause's table. Fails if sampled_slots is moved to default's true row.
